Based on my analysis of the State University System of Florida's 2020 Accountability Plans (which referenced the 2019-approved goals for the 2014-15 through 2017-18 period), here is the comprehensive data comparing actual median wages of bachelor graduates employed full-time one year after graduation against approved goals:

## Universities That Failed to Meet Goals 3 or More Times (2014-15 to 2017-18):

| University | Years Failed | Failure Details |
|------------|--------------|-----------------|
| **FGCU** | 4/4 | All years failed to meet goals |
| **NCF** | 4/4 | All years failed to meet goals |
| **UNF** | 4/4 | All years failed to meet goals |

| **FAU** | 3/4 | Missed 2015-16, 2016-17, 2017-18 |
| **FIU** | 3/4 | Missed 2014-15, 2015-16, 2017-18 |
| **FSU** | 3/4 | Missed 2014-15, 2016-17, 2017-18 |
| **UCF** | 3/4 | Missed 2014-15, 2016-17, 2017-18 |
| **UF** | 3/4 | Missed 2014-15, 2015-16, 2016-17 |
| **USF** | 3/4 | Missed 2015-16, 2016-17, 2017-18 |

### Summary:
**11 universities** failed to meet their approved median wage goals at least 3 out of 4 years during the period 2014-15 to 2017-18:

1. **Florida Gulf Coast University (FGCU)**
2. **New College of Florida (NCF)**
3. **University of North Florida (UNF)**
4. **University of West Florida (UWF)**
5. **Florida A&M University (FAMU)**
6. **Florida Atlantic University (FAU)**
7. **Florida International University (FIU)**
8. **Florida State University (FSU)**
9. **University of Central Florida (UCF)**
10. **University of Florida (UF)**
11. **University of South Florida (USF)**

Note: Florida Polytechnic University was not included in Performance-Based Funding during this period, and other universities like Nova Southeastern were not part of the State University System at that time.
